hypothesis_text: In multi-agent autonomous-research settings, the hypotheses generated by a retrieval-augmented worker are LESS diverse than those from a no-retrieval worker, because shared retrieval state acts as a coordination signal that pulls workers toward the same prior-art-anchored framing.
prior_art_summary: RAG literature universally argues retrieval improves grounding and quality; diversity-reducing effect at the multi-worker level is not a hypothesis we have seen in published RAG or multi-agent work.
rationale: Predicts a counter-intuitive emergent effect of shared retrieval at the worker-pool level. High novelty.
